A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same s3 research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original QA experiments, component ablations, a 1,000-sample human annotation study and extended-training results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and outcomes, including the main benchmark results and appendix studies.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 reorders the displayed cycle to retrieval, selection, stopping and next-query generation. This restates the existing behavior documented by v1’s initialization and unchanged Figure 11 prompt. The searcher/generator architecture, GBR reward and PPO optimization remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions train on NQ and HotpotQA and evaluate the same six general-domain and five MIRAGE medical QA datasets. The Wikipedia-only and combined Wikipedia/PubMed/textbook corpus settings are retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons in Tables 1–2 retain the same baseline membership and model variants, including Search-R1, IRCoT, Search-o1 and DeepRetrieval. Shortening the baseline description does not remove evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Reported sample sizes, models, training budgets and experimental configurations remain unchanged. The added statement about LLMJudge for binary test questions supplies previously unstated evaluation detail; it does not report a switch from an earlier procedure.

E4.justification: The retrieval/turn sensitivity study, component and reward ablations, human-alignment study, 300-step scalability study and search-trajectory example are retained. No new robustness test or supplementary analysis is added.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 continue to report averages over three runs. There are no additions or revisions to seed information, uncertainty estimates or significance testing; parenthesized table scores remain exact-match results.

E6.justification: Matched table entries and plotted results are unchanged, including Claude-3-Haiku averages of 58.9 in Table 1 and 76.6 with the combined medical corpus in Table 2. Appendix ablation, human-alignment, scalability and example outcomes also match.

T1.justification: The GBR definition, PPO objective and GenAcc formula remain unchanged. The loop’s query-index adjustment accompanies its reordered explanation, without introducing a new mathematical result, assumption or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about modular search-only optimization, GBR, compatibility with frozen generators and strong performance using 2.4k training examples.

C2.justification: Figure 12’s expanded caption explains that suppressing reasoning text prevents incidental gold-answer mentions from producing misleading correctness judgments. This adds a specific evaluation failure-mode explanation; the existing result interpretations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies that yes/no and true/false test questions are evaluated with LLMJudge. The implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, prompt bodies and code/data access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Su et al. (2025), Crossing the Reward Bridge, when introducing reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. The introductory period labels change from RL-Zero to RLVR, while the substantive positioning against prior retrieval methods is retained.

P1.justification: Targeted edits revise terminology and the loop explanation, shorten the baseline paragraph, add acknowledgments and update the affiliation footnote. The appendix contents correctly label Prompts as C and Scalability Study as D; the overall organization is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2’s period labels, Figure 4’s search-agent label and caption, and Figure 11’s title are revised. Figure 12 gains explanatory caption text, with modest layout reflow. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 improves evaluation transparency by specifying binary-question judging and explaining the existing direct-answer safeguard. Corrected appendix navigation and targeted presentation edits also help readers. These are limited documentation gains: the method, empirical evidence and principal conclusions remain unchanged.
